title: Tucatinib and trastuzumab in HER3-mutant and HER2-not amplified metastatic breast cancer
official: "H3RAKLES": Tucatinib and trastuzumab in HER3-mutant and HER2-not amplified metastatic breast cancer
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate that ERBB3 mutations are actionable in breast cancer in terms of 24 weeks clinical benefit rate
conditions: HER3-mutant and HER2-not amplified metastatic breast cancer

interventions.name: Ogivri 150 mg powder for concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Molecular screening step: availability of a formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) block with >10% tumor tissue (it is recommended to provide the most recently collected tumor sample).
2. Having received ≥ 2 previous chemotherapy lines for advanced breast cancer
3. Class IV or V somatic ERBB3 mutation as determined on a tumor sample obtained during the molecular screening step
4. ECOG performance status ≤ 2
5. Evaluable disease, per RECIST v1.1 inclusion criteria
6. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥50% as assessed by echocardiogram (ECHO) or multiple-gated acquisition scan (MUGA) documented within 4 weeks prior to first dose of study treatment
7. Adequate organ function: a.Creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min as calculated per institutional guidelines; b.Total bilirubin ≤1.5 X upper limit of normal (ULN), except for patients with known Gilbert’s disease, who may enroll if the conjugated bilirubin is ≤1.5 X ULN; c.Transaminases (aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase) ≤ 2.5 X ULN (≤ 5 X ULN if the patient has liver metastases)
8. Women of childbearing potential (WCBP) must have a negative serum pregnancy test < 7 days prior to first dose of treatment. A woman is considered of childbearing potential following menarche and until becoming post-menopausal unless permanently sterile. A postmenopausal state is defined as the absence of menses for 12 months without an alternative cause.
9. WCBP (as defined above) and men with partners of childbearing potential must agree to use a highly effective birth control method during the study and for 3 months after completion of investigational treatment.
10. Patients should be eligible for the treatment step according to the investigator’s opinion.
11. Patients must be covered by a health insurance plan.
12. Molecular screening step: the tumor sample must have been obtained less than 5 years before inclusion
13. Patients able to provide signed informed consent.
14. Molecular screening step: prior signature of a written informed molecular screening consent.
15. Molecular screening step: patients should be eligible for the treatment step according to the investigator’s opinion.
16. Molecular screening step: patients must be covered by a health insurance plan.
17. Molecular screening step: patients able to provide signed informed consent.
18. Age ≥ 18 years
19. Metastatic or unresectable breast cancer
20. HER2-negative (defined as having an IHC 0+, IHC 1+, or IHC 2+ and ISH non-amplified, per ASCO/CAP guidelines) on last assessable tumor sample
Exclusion criteria:
1. Having received any prior treatment targeting HER2. Prior treatment with trastuzumab deruxtecan is allowed, per label, in patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer (IHC 1+ or 2+, ISH non-amplified)
2. Leptomeningeal metastases
3. Major surgery (including surgery of brain metastases) < 21 days prior to first dose of treatment
4. Evidence within 2 years of the start of study treatment of another malignancy that required systemic treatment
5. Have known myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 24 weeks prior to first dose of study treatment
6. Have clinically significant cardiopulmonary disease such as: • Ventricular arrhythmia requiring therapy,  • Uncontrolled hypertension (defined as persistent systolic blood pressure >150 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure > 100 mm Hg on antihy) due to complications of advanced malignancy, • Hypoxia requiring supplementary oxygen therapy except when oxygen therapy is needed only for obstructive sleep apnea,  • Presence of ≥ Grade 2 QTc prolongation on screening ECG,  • Conditions potentially resulting in drug-induced prolongation of the QT interval or torsade de pointes: o Congenital or acquired long QT syndrome,  o	Family history of sudden death,  o History of previous drug-induced QT prolongation,  o	Current use of medications with known and accepted associated risk of QT prolongation
7. Are known carriers of active Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C or have other known chronic liver disease
8. Are known to be positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)
9. Altered mental status or psychiatric disorder that, in the opinion of the investigator, would preclude a valid patient informed consent.
10. Patients who have difficulty undergoing trial procedures for geographic, social or psychological reasons
11. Person deprived of liberty or under guardianship
12. History of allergic reactions to trastuzumab or tucatinib or chemically similar drugs
13. Patients who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning a pregnancy from time of informed consent until 7 months after the final dose of study drug
14. Inability to swallow pills or having a significant gastro-intestinal disease or a history of surgery which would preclude the adequate oral absorption of medications
15. Having used a strong CYP2C8 inhibitor within a duration of 5 half-lives prior to the first dose of study treatment, or have used a strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inducer within 5 days prior to first dose of study treatment (see Appendix B and Appendix C)
16. Treatment with any systemic anti-cancer therapy (including hormonal therapy), non-central nervous system (CNS) radiation, or experimental agent ≤ 3 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment, except gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists
17. Participation in another interventional clinical trial.
18. Symptomatic and untreated brain metastases or brain metastases requiring urgent treatment, or brain metastases requiring a dose > 2 mg of dexamethasone (or equivalent)
19. Whole brain radiotherapy < 21 days prior to first dose of treatment, stereotactic radiotherapy < 7 days prior to first dose of treatment
